title: Exceptional activated mode theory for generalized real-complex transitions
authors: Mengjie Yang, Alexander N. Poddubny, Ching Hua Lee
abstract: Real-to-complex spectral transitions mark the onset of amplification in non-Hermitian systems, but their thresholds are often treated as model-specific quantities. Here we develop a general, non-perturbative activated-mode principle that governs the real-to-complex threshold across broad classes of non-Hermitian systems. A central insight is that only a small Hilbert subspace is ``activated" at the transition onset, which can be variationally determined through the competition between spectral detuning and mode-level projected non-Hermitian couplings. The result is a closed-form exceptional-activation condition for arbitrarily large ``disturbances", rather than a perturbative estimate. We apply our framework to three contrasting illustrative problems, establishing (i) a closed-form threshold for critical non-Hermitian skin amplification at \emph{all} system sizes; (ii) a new link between impurity tunneling threshold and exceptional point switching; and (iii) activation channel switching without underlying topological phase transition. Overall, our findings recast real-to-complex transitions as generic mode-selection problems independent of any specific symmetry.
summary: The authors introduce an activated-mode principle to universally describe the critical threshold where non-Hermitian spectra transition from real to complex values. By identifying a minimal 'activated' subspace pair, they derive a closed-form condition that governs this onset across diverse physical models. This framework successfully predicts crossover regimes and channel switching without relying on specific symmetries or perturbative assumptions.
main_problem: The paper develops a general, non-perturbative activated-mode principle to govern the critical threshold for real-to-complex spectral transitions in non-Hermitian systems.
main_result: It establishes a unified, closed-form condition ($\lambda_c = \Delta_{	ext{act}} / G_{	ext{act}}$) that determines the transition onset by finding the minimum threshold across all possible active Hilbert subspaces.
method: The theory involves pair-resolved analysis of the exceptional point (EP) condition on a small, 'activated' subspace, avoiding perturbative expansions in system parameters.
model_or_system: The framework is applied to broad classes of non-Hermitian systems, including coupled Hatano-Nelson chains, topological SSH models with gain/loss, and impurity-modified lattices.
key_observables: Critical coupling strength ($\lambda_c$), spectral detuning ($\Delta E_{ij}$), and projected activation strength ($G_{	ext{act}}$).
important_parameters: System size (L), impurity strength ($\mu$), and the ratio of hopping parameters in SSH models.
main_assumptions: The theory assumes that the transition is governed by a small, variationally determined active subspace pair, and $H_0$ is diagonalizable in the spectral window.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the activated mode mechanism (EP competition), show the agreement between derived closed-form thresholds and numerical results for cNHSE models, and track how the 'winning' active channel switches as a function of external parameters ($\mu$).
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the general non-perturbative principle to applying it sequentially to specific physical realizations: first, generic NHSE systems; second, impurity-modified OBC/PBC setups; and finally, analyzing complex switching behavior in SSH chains.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, generalized analytical tool for understanding spectral singularities (like EPs) that govern system stability or amplification onset in open quantum systems, applicable far beyond simple perturbation theory.
